title: Credential traffic diagnostics and UI proposals
summary: Working notes and low-fi wireframe proposals for a credential-level diagnostics panel: how to surface per-credential/per-route throttle events, quota exhaustion reasons, and quick triage steps for customers and support engineers.
background: Support and SRE have asked for a single place in the console where a customer or SE can rapidly understand why a key started getting 429s or perceived slowdowns. Current signal is scattered across the usage chart, alerts, and audit logs. This doc sketches a focused panel and interaction flows to reduce time-to-resolution.
goals: 1) Reduce support TTR for throttle incidents. 2) Make quota and rate-limit rules explainable to non-engineers. 3) Provide safe self-service remediation (adjust route priority, request temporary burst, or open support with pre-populated context).
heuristics: - Keep primary explanation < 3 sentences. - Default to conservative remediation suggestions. - Avoid exposing internal SLO math but show actionable knobs. - Preserve security: only show credential-scoped data to owners and collaborators.
proposed_wires:
Top-level layout (left to right): [Credential selector dropdown] | [Summary card: current state, active rules, last 24h 429 count] | [Traffic timeline with overlayed quota windows] | [Action pane with quick remediation buttons].
Low-fi notes: timeline should allow toggling 'by route' vs 'by method' and zoom to incident window. Summary card contains computed cause (eg: 'burst exceeded: route xyz') with confidence badge (high/medium/low). Action pane includes: 'Request short burst', 'Open support ticket (with diagnostics)', 'Enable fallback model/route'.
data_matrix: Columns: metric, shortlist, source, confidence, recommended-action. Example row: '429s per min', 'spike at 10:42-10:46', 'rate-limit-enforcer (us-east-1)', 'high', 'request burst / apply temporary quota'. This sheet will be a living reference for the UI to map signals to human-friendly text.
ux_scenarios: 1) Developer: sees 429s after deploy, opens diagnostics, filters to their credential, sees spike localized to one route, clicks 'Enable fallback route' and verifies reduction in observed 429s. 2) Support engineer: customer file attached, opens pre-populated ticket payload from 'Open support' button with timeline and top three correlated anomalies. 3) Platform admin: wants to see which credentials are the largest outliers over last 7 days and export CSV for cost review.
micro_interactions: - Hover on the timeline point shows per-route breakdown and top contributing tokens. - 'Confidence' badge expands into a short explanation of which rule matched. - Clicking 'Request short burst' opens a modal with estimated cost impact and ETA to approve. - Buttons disabled if customer lacks permissions with tooltip 'contact owner'.
metrics_and_alerts: Suggested alerts to tie into panel: 1) credential-429-rate > threshold (auto-populate timeline). 2) sustained-queue-latency > SLO (link to traces). 3) burst-consumption > 80% of quota (suggest pre-emptive burst request). Each alert should map to suggested next steps shown in the panel.
open_questions: What exact signal set should the confidence engine aggregate from (429s, observed latency, queue length, kernel OOMs, fallback invocations)?
Should 'Request short burst' be automated (self-serve) for paid tiers, or routed to SE approval?
Do we need separate views for org-admin vs credential-owner (and what fields are sensitive)?
How to represent shared credentials used by multiple teams (attribution)?
What retention window for timeline and exports (30d, 90d)?
edge_cases_and_notes:
- In many incidents 429s are downstream/backpressure not our rate-limit (eg model server slow). Need a clear signal to say 'likely server backpressure' vs 'rate-limit triggered'.
- Avoid creating a UI that encourages customers to just raise quota without understanding load patterns. Include friction (cost estimate) on any self-serve increase.
- Quick export should include anonymized token counts when sharing debug traces with third parties.
next_steps: 1) Sync with SRE and support (Rajan) to lock down the minimal signal set. 2) Product-design spike: create hi-fi mockups for the credential panel (Evelyn). 3) Engineering spike to validate feasible query patterns and latency for the timeline (Luis). 4) Add Linear ticket to propose API endpoint for the diagnostics payload and RBAC checks.
todo: - Draft API contract for diagnostics payload. - Prototype timeline with sampled data (not production). - Run 3 customer interviews (existing enterprise customers) to validate language and trust of confidence badges.
notes_to_self: Remember: lean on existing 'alerts' infra; prefer to reuse alert ids rather than creating duplicate rules. Keep the first iteration read-only except for safe actions (request burst, open ticket).
audit_trail_hint: Include a small 'history' tab listing who triggered actions (request burst, enabled fallback) and when; this is important for billing disputes.
